title: Flowers at the Magic Pond: A Puzzle and the Pattern Hiding Inside It
summary: A recreational mathematics article for school students and teachers: a flower puzzle at a magic pond, worked backwards into a general rule built on geometric series.

title: Cotton-Origin-Linked Tariff Preferences and Bangladesh's Apparel Export Diversification to Brazil: A Policy Commentary
summary: A policy commentary on the BGMEA proposal to link verified Brazilian cotton to preferential tariff access for Bangladeshi garments in Brazil, and the traceability, pricing, and negotiation conditions it would need to work.

title: Your Cotton May Be Safe Under EUDR. Your Entire Bill of Materials May Not Be: A Component-Level Perspective for Apparel Supply Chains
summary: Why a cotton garment can still fall under EUDR through its trims, rubber, wood, and packaging, and how a component-level BOM review helps sourcing teams screen risk before the 2026–27 deadlines.

title: From the Discharge Pipe to the Sludge Cake: A Sourcing and Policy Perspective on the Shift from Wastewater to Sludge Governance in Bangladesh's Apparel Industry
summary: Why apparel compliance is moving from treated wastewater to the sludge it leaves behind, and what ZDHC's shift means for Bangladesh's hazardous-waste infrastructure and sourcing risk.

title: Why Bangladesh's Costing Sheets Still Begin With Cotton: Fiscal Signals, the Man-Made Fibre Transition, and the Coordination Problem in Apparel Sourcing
summary: Why Bangladesh's shift to man-made fibres is stuck on a coordination problem, read through the FY2026–27 budget signals on MMF yarn VAT and polyester raw material duties.
